text: What should Morgan Street position as the first shared-services AI lighthouse and why?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Lakeshore Holdings should position Legal Contract Intake as its first shared-services AI lighthouse at Morgan Street — and the tenant evidence makes the case clearly. The loaded context identifies Legal Contract Intake as the single workflow where Legal Ops, Deputy GC, Procurement, Finance Controls, IT/Data, Security, and OpCo requestors all intersect.
That cross-functional density is exactly what you want in a lighthouse: one workflow that demonstrates AI value across multiple stakeholder groups simultaneously, rather than solving a siloed problem that only one team sees. Three reasons this is the right first bet: (1) Cross-functional visibility. A lighthouse needs an audience.
Contract intake touches every major shared-services function at the holdco level, so a win here is visible to CFO, GC, and OpCo leadership in a single motion. (2) Finance has already stress-tested the value claim.
The CFO's office reduced the initial assumption to 8–12% cycle-time improvement with outside counsel avoidance treated as directional — not hard savings. That discipline means the business case is defensible, not inflated. A lighthouse that survives finance scrutiny is far more credible than one built on vendor projections. (3) The workflow is documentable.
Contract intake is process-bounded and leaves an artifact trail — intake forms, routing decisions, review cycles, approvals. That makes it tractable for AI augmentation (classification, routing, extraction, status summarization) without requiring a clean enterprise data foundation first.
